write.markdown:
# How automated backups work

Automated backups copy selected data on a schedule. [[claim:backup-copy]] A job combines a source, a destination, a schedule, and a retention policy. These are useful starting points when documenting a backup workflow. This demonstration uses [project-authored backup notes](https://example.com/demo/backup-notes), rather than a claim of independent product testing.

## Plan the copy

Identify the data to preserve and the storage location that will hold the copy. Document when the job runs and how long older copies remain available. Keeping a copy on a separate device reduces dependence on the original device. Different systems can need different schedules, so write the requirements down before choosing a schedule.

## Check recovery

Restore tests check whether a saved copy can be read and used. [[claim:restore-test]] A completed copy operation alone does not establish successful recovery. Keep recovery instructions next to the backup configuration and identify who can access the required decryption keys.

## Make failures visible

Monitoring records when a backup starts, finishes, or fails. [[claim:monitoring]] A missed job should be visible to the person responsible for recovery. Review the logs together with the retention policy and recovery objectives. The practical next step is to document a small restore exercise and have a person review the result.
